gate.rule: Pass only if all three hold for the adstock-saturation MMM (geometric adstock carryover with Hill saturation), fixed before results as the headline: (1) the 95% bootstrap interval on holdout weekly revenue R^2 has a lower bound above 0.75; (2) the rank correlation (Spearman rho) between estimated channel marginal ROIs and true marginal ROIs is at least 0.80; (3) the holdout incremental revenue under the headline model's recommended budget allocation beats the naive linear allocation by at least 5%.

ignoring_adstock.finding: Naive linear regression assumes zero carryover decay (half-life 0.0 weeks), missing TV's multi-week brand persistence (true half-life 1.36 weeks).

ignoring_saturation.finding: Under linear assumptions, doubling Search spend projects a 2.00x revenue increase, whereas true Hill diminishing returns yield diminishing marginal return.

correlated_spend_bias.finding: TV and Search spend are synchronized; naive OLS suffers multicollinearity, inverting Search's slope and cutting Search spend to minimum compared to balanced MMM allocation.

caveats: All data is generated by an econometric simulator with known adstock and Hill saturation.
Real marketing channels exhibit competitive bidding dynamics and creative fatigue not modeled here.
Observation noise is additive Gaussian without macroeconomic supply shocks or stock-outs.
Bootstrap intervals resample holdout weeks; they do not cover structural shifts in channel effectiveness.
